transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess I’m here because I can’t stop worrying about this scar on my wrist. I know it’s probably not as bad as it looks to me, but when I’m at church or playing bridge, I feel like everyone’s eyes go right to it, like it’s the first thing they notice about me now.
Is it just the scar on your wrist that you worry about, or are there other parts of your body that you're concerned with as well?

Mostly it’s the scar on my wrist. I know it probably doesn’t look as bad to other people as it does to me, but when I’m at church or playing bridge, I keep feeling like people notice it right away. Like their eyes go straight to it.
Have you ever found yourself worrying about other parts of your body in the past?

No, not really. In the past I didn’t worry much about other parts of my body. It’s mainly this scar on my wrist now. I know it probably isn’t as noticeable as it feels to me, but when I’m at church or playing bridge, I just feel like people’s eyes go right to it.
Do you find yourself repeatedly checking the scar on your wrist?

Yes. Before I leave the house, I usually check it in the hall mirror a few times. I’ll try different sleeves, or put on a bracelet to see if it covers it better. Sometimes I ask my husband if it looks obvious, even though he always says it’s barely noticeable.
Do you ever find yourself performing specific rituals or behaviors to try and reduce your worry about the scar?

Yes, I guess I do. Before I leave the house, I’ll check my wrist in the hall mirror a few times, and I’ll try different sleeves or maybe a bracelet to cover it. Sometimes I ask my husband if it looks obvious, even though he always tells me it’s barely there.
Has your worry about the scar on your wrist interfered with your daily activities or relationships in any way?

Yes, it has some. I’ve been late turning in my bookkeeping work because I get caught up checking my wrist and trying to cover it. And I’ve skipped a few choir things and theater volunteer commitments because I just didn’t want people noticing it.
How distressed do you feel when you think about the scar on your wrist?

It does upset me, more than I think it probably should. I know the scar is probably not as bad as it looks to me, but when I’m at church or playing bridge, I feel like people’s eyes go right to it—like it’s the first thing they notice about me now.
Have you avoided any social interactions or activities because of your concerns about the scar on your wrist?

Yes. I’ve skipped some choir practices and theater volunteer things because I was too worried people would notice my wrist. And with work, I’ve even been late turning in bookkeeping because I get caught up trying to cover it or make sure it doesn’t show.
Has your worry about the scar on your wrist affected your relationship with your husband or other family members?

A little, yes. I think it’s more shown up in the things I don’t do—I’ve been late with my bookkeeping work because I get stuck trying to make sure my wrist is covered, and I’ve skipped some choir and theater volunteer things. With my family, it’s mostly that I get distracted or avoid going places if I think people might notice it.
Do you think your worry about the scar is reasonable, or does it feel like it's more bothersome to you than it should be to someone else in your situation?

I think it’s probably more bothersome to me than it would be to someone else. I can tell myself the scar isn’t really that bad, but then when I’m at church or playing bridge, I start feeling like everyone is looking right at my wrist, like it’s the first thing they notice about me.
Have you considered seeking any treatment or professional help specifically for your concerns about the scar on your wrist?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t gone to anyone specifically about the scar, no. I guess I’ve mostly just been trying to handle it myself.
Have you noticed any impact on your overall quality of life due to your concerns about the scar?

Yes, it has, though I guess not in a huge way. I’ve been late getting some bookkeeping work turned in because I get caught up trying to make sure my wrist is covered or won’t be noticed. And I’ve skipped a few choir and theater volunteer commitments for the same reason. It just gets in the way more than I’d like.
Have you felt like your worry about the scar has taken over your life or significantly affected your ability to enjoy things you used to?

I wouldn’t say it’s taken over my whole life, no. But it has definitely gotten in the way. I’ve been late with bookkeeping work because I get caught up trying to cover my wrist, and I’ve skipped some choir and theater volunteer things because I was worried people would notice it. So, yes, it has affected things I normally enjoy.
Have you felt like your worry about the scar has caused problems in your relationships with friends or family members?

Not really with friends or family, at least not directly. It’s more that I’ve missed some choir and theater volunteer things, and I’ve been late with bookkeeping work because I get too caught up making sure my wrist won’t be noticed. So it affects what I show up for, more than arguments or anything like that.
Have you felt like your worry about the scar has caused you significant distress or impairment in your daily life?

Yes, I’d say it has, though maybe mildly. I get so caught up trying to make sure my wrist won’t be noticed that I’ve been late turning in bookkeeping work, and I’ve skipped some choir and theater volunteer commitments because of it. It’s not ruining everything, but it does interfere with my day-to-day life.
Is your worry about the scar on your wrist ever about anything other than how it looks to others?

No, not really. It’s mostly about how it looks and what I think other people see. I know the scar probably isn’t as bad as it seems to me, but if I’m at church or playing bridge, I feel like everyone’s eyes go right to my wrist, like that’s the first thing they notice about me now.
Would you say that your worry about the scar has caused you more than mild distress?

I think it’s more on the mild side, honestly. It does bother me, and it gets in the way some—I’ve been late with bookkeeping work and skipped choir or theater volunteer things because I’m fussing over whether my wrist will show. But I wouldn’t say it’s more than mild distress.
Is your worry about the scar mostly about it making you look unattractive to others?

Yes, mostly. I know the scar on my wrist probably doesn’t look as bad as it feels to me, but when I’m at church or playing bridge, I keep thinking everyone’s eyes go right to it, like it’s the first thing they notice about me now.
Is your worry about the scar mostly about its impact on your overall attractiveness or is it about something specific like its size, shape, or color?

It’s more specific to the scar, I think—how it looks on my wrist. I know it’s probably not as bad as it seems to me, but when I’m at church or playing bridge, I feel like people’s eyes go right to it, like it’s the first thing they notice.
